prerequisites: Completion of the study entry and orientation phase

learning_outcomes.text: Students have in-depth knowledge of the fundamental concepts, components, and operating principles of energy and drive technology and are able to apply them to solve problems in application.
Students possess basic knowledge of applied robotics and can plan and safely use robotic systems, e.g., for automating technical processes. They can implement simple tasks on industrial robots.
Students are familiar with practical problems in industrial mechatronics and materials science.

syllabus_topics: VO Electrical Energy and Drive Technology: Energy and power in electrical circuits; Energy provision; Fundamentals of electrical power supply networks and systems; Tasks and structures of transmission and distribution networks; Transformers; Insulation and high-voltage technology; Synchronous and asynchronous machines; Characteristics of power and work machines; Electrical drives using DC and AC machines; Fundamentals of drive control and regulation;
UE Electrical Energy and Drive Technology: Accompanying exercises for the lecture;

PR Applied Robotics: Application-oriented aspects of robotics, e.g., safety, human-machine interface, human-robot collaboration, programming, path interpolation, PTP control, bus systems, synchronization, grippers, drives and measurement technology; Modeling and identification of mechatronic systems; Creation of a dynamic model of the robot considering drive, control and damping; Performing practical exercises with mobile and stationary robots;
PR Laboratory Industrial Mechatronics and Materials Science: Projects/laboratory internships on selected topics in industrial mechatronics and materials science;
